restoration_note: Teaching describes the four great works of Sin (the proprium's complete fourfold extension: appetite, fornication, possession/boasting, war/tyranny) set against the single saving work of the Apostle — the separation of Light from Darkness received as faith and obedience. Restorations are heavily constrained by (1) the repeating enumerative formula 'the Nth matter is X', (2) the visible partial traces, (3) the standard ordinal/relative/article completions split across line breaks, and (4) the closing parallel triplet 'in the only-begottenness, in the godhead, with the obedience.' Several medium lacunae in the second-work passage (around fornication) and in the closing 'ⲧⲉ___ ' phrase before ⲙⲛⲧⲙⲟⲛⲟⲅⲉⲛⲏⲥ remained too damaged to fix without invention; these are honestly marked unrestorable.

restorations.basis: Editor restoration completing ⲩⲧⲁⲩ (Lycopolitan 'four'); the chapter is structured around the fourfold catalogue of great works.
Editor restoration; the chapter's enumerated unit is ⲡⲩⲧⲁⲩ ⲛ̄ⲛⲁⲃ ⲛϩⲱⲃ ('four great matters'), repeated explicitly in section 4523.
Editor restoration completing ϣⲟⲟⲡ; partial ϣ visible; the relative formula 'matters that exist in the cosmos' fits the syntax.
Editor restoration: 'all the men of the earth kill one another for them' — repeats the chapter title formula and matches the slaughtering motif of section 4525.
Editor restoration: ⲧⲧϣⲁⲣⲡ (Lyc fem ordinal) opens the enumeration of the four works, paralleled by ⲧⲧⲙⲁϩⲥⲛⲉⲩ, ⲧⲧⲙⲁϩϣⲁⲙⲧ, ⲧⲧⲙⲁϩⲩⲧⲁⲩ in following sections.

Editor tentative restoration; 'care of the mouth, that they shall eat...' fits the first work as appetite/gluttony — self-love through the gate of taste; matches Coptic register for preoccupation with food.
Editor restoration ϩⲁ ⲡϯⲟⲩⲱ ('for the sustenance of their body'); ϯⲟⲩⲱ matches the bodily-nourishment register and completes the syntactic frame.
Editor restoration completing ⲧⲧⲙⲁϩⲥⲛⲉⲩ (Lyc fem ordinal 'second'); opens the second work in the parallel enumeration.
Editor restoration completing ⲧⲥⲩⲛⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ (Greek συνουσία 'sexual intercourse'); matches the second matter's content (fornication / disordered conjunction of bodies).

Ten characters between ⲧⲥⲩⲛⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ and ⲡⲟⲣⲛⲓⲁ; could be a connector + qualifier ('and the practice of', 'in the work of'), but multiple plausible Coptic fills exist with no decisive trace or formula. Honest non-restoration.

Three chars opening a list; 'ⲙⲛ̄ ⲛ̄ⲛⲕⲁ' ('and the things of fornication') is the most natural connector continuing the enumeration of fornication's modes. Fits the structural register of the second work.
Three chars binding 'the things' to 'fornication' as genitive/possessive; ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ is the standard Coptic relator and fits the slot exactly.
Two chars introducing the antithetic pair 'males with females'; ⲙⲛ̄ is the standard conjunction and matches the parallel ⲙⲛ̄ ⲛⲥϩⲓⲙⲉ that follows.
Editor restoration completing the antithetic pair 'males with females' (ⲛϩⲁⲩⲧ ⲙⲛ ⲛⲥϩⲓⲙⲉ); standard Manichaean register for sexual sin.
Editor restoration completing ⲡⲭⲣⲏⲙⲁ (Greek χρῆμα) + connector ⲙⲛ̄; pairs with ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲣⲙⲙⲁⲟ ('wealth') that follows, the third work being the love of possession.

Four chars between 'property and' and 'the wealth which they desire'; could be ⲡⲉⲁⲩ ('glory'), ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲃ-related ('gold'), or another paired vice — multiple plausible fills exist with no decisive trace. Honest non-restoration.
Editor restoration of ⲡⲉⲧ- relative substantive; standard Coptic relative construction continuing the description of wealth.

Four chars including article; 'on account of the things by their hand' — what they have obtained — fits the boasting motif and the third work of possession. Coptic ⲛ̄ⲕⲁ is the standard term for material possessions.
Editor restoration completing ⲛϥⲓⲗⲟⲛⲓⲕⲓⲁ (Greek φιλονικία 'rivalry/contentiousness'); standard early Christian moral-vice term paired with πόλεμος ('war').
One char between ⲗⲉⲃ (end of previous line) and visible ⲉ; reconstructs ⲗⲉⲃⲏⲉ/ⲗⲏⲃⲉ ('frenzy'), the noun governed by ⲛϥⲓⲗⲟⲛⲓⲕⲓⲁ; partial ⲉ visible.
Editor restoration completing ⲙⲛ̄ ('with'); repeats the formula ⲙⲛ̄ ⲛⲉⲩⲉⲣⲏⲩ ('with one another') from the same line.
Editor restoration completing ⲛⲉⲩⲉⲣⲏⲩ ('one another'); standard formula in the war-passage describing mutual prevailing.
Editor restoration completing ⲛⲉⲧϣⲟⲟⲡ ('who exist'); relative substantive describing those who pursue the four works, paralleled in section 4524.
Editor restoration of preposition phrase ϩⲙ̄ ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ ('in the cosmos'); standard formula echoing section 4509.

Two chars after ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ ⲛ̄; reconstructs start of ⲣⲱⲙⲉ ('men') split across line break with {25}=ⲙ continuing it on next line; matches phrase 'cosmos of men' echoing 'world of all men' in section 4523.
One char with partial ⲉ visible; completes ⲣⲱⲙⲉ split across line break from {24}=ⲣⲱ; the visible ⲉ is the final letter of ⲣⲱⲙⲉ.
Eight chars; could echo 'a name' (ⲟⲩⲣⲉⲛ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ) from section 4522 ('that they may take a name'), but other plausible fills exist with no decisive trace. Honest non-restoration.
Editor restoration; ϩⲛⲁ- as Lyc 3pl future prefix yielding ϩⲛⲁϫⲓ ('they shall receive a faith and thanksgiving').
Editor restoration of ⲡⲓⲥⲉⲓⲛⲉ ('this likeness') split across line break; the lexicon-fixed term ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ = 'likeness' (the icon of separation brought by the Apostle).

Three chars after ⲧⲉ at end of line, paired with {30} of two chars at start of next line, all preceding 'in the only-begottenness, in the godhead, with the obedience.' The combined word ⲧⲉ_____ is uncertain — could be ⲧⲡⲣⲟⲃⲟⲗⲏ (emanation) or another abstract — without decisive trace. Honest non-restoration.
Two chars continuing the broken word from {29}; same uncertainty applies. Honest non-restoration.
Editor restoration completing ⲧⲙ̄ⲛⲧⲥⲧⲙⲏⲧ ('the obedience') split across line break; the closing faculty in the Hearing-answers-Call register.
Editor restoration completing ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ ('all'); modifies ⲣⲱⲙⲉ — 'exalted far more than all men' — closes the arc by lifting the soul above the cosmos of self-love.
